title: Cryogenic Storage Tank

introduction.definition: A full-containment LNG tank stores liquefied natural gas at about −162 °C. A 9 % nickel inner tank holds the liquid, thick insulation limits heat leak, and a pre-stressed concrete outer tank can contain liquid and vapour if the inner tank fails. In-tank pumps send LNG out through the roof; boil-off gas is recovered.

classification.type: Full-containment LNG tank with suspended deck

introduction.summary: A full-containment LNG tank stores liquefied natural gas at about −162 °C. An inner tank of 9 % nickel steel holds the liquid; thick insulation limits heat leak; an outer pre-stressed concrete wall and roof can contain the liquid and vapour if the inner tank leaks. Pumps in columns send LNG out from the top, and boil-off gas is removed and recovered.

video_tutorials.title: Cryogenic Storage Tank — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Cryogenic Storage Tank.
A full-containment LNG tank stores liquefied natural gas at about −162 °C.
A 9 % nickel inner tank holds the liquid, thick insulation limits heat leak, and a pre-stressed concrete outer tank can contain liquid and vapour if the inner tank fails.
In-tank pumps send LNG out through the roof; boil-off gas is recovered.
Typical applications include LNG import/export terminals; peak-shaving plants; liquid nitrogen/oxygen/argon storage (smaller, vacuum-insulated); ethylene storage.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: In-Tank Submerged Pumps in Pump Columns (no bottom penetrations).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Cryogenic Storage Tank — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Cryogenic Storage Tank.
Monitor level, temperature/density profiles, BOG.
Test in-tank pumps (pull via columns).
Inspection at decommissioning only (rare).
Watch for rollover: sudden large BOG release. Common cause: stratification of different-density LNG.
Watch for cold spots on outer wall: thermography anomaly. Common cause: insulation defect.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
